title: Are the springtails dying out?
goal: Keep every story whose usual range includes 5. A usual range is the low end to the high end that holds 9 in 10 or more of the counts a story gives in six jars, worked out exactly. A fit is not proof: it only shows which stories the notebook's count fits.
story: The report says dying out. Which story could give the notebook's 5 of 6? Same idea as Lesson 6, new names: guesses is now stories, and seen_count is now observed_count.

dictionary.means: three guesses about the springtails, one row each: story, p (the chance one jar has springtails), lower and upper (the usual range of the count in six jars). Julia's word: a DataFrame.
the notebook's count: 5 jars with springtails out of 6
a rule inside a column's brackets keeps the values where it is true: the names of the stories with p of 0.5 or less. Julia's word: a boolean mask on a Vector.
6: the number of jars in the notebook. Each story's usual range is a count out of these 6.

challenges.prompt: The table stories lists three guesses, each with a usual range from lower to upper. Show every story whose range includes the notebook's 5 (the name observed_count), with all four columns: story, p, lower, upper.
hints: A story fits when its lower end is at most the count and the count is at most its upper end. Both ends count.

feedback.pass: Coin flip and Thriving fit: 5 is inside both usual ranges. Dying out stops before 5.

challenges.prompt: Which story's usual range ends at 4 or lower, so 5 lies outside it? Show its row with all four columns.
hints: Keep the rows whose upper end is at most 4. The rule goes before the comma in the square brackets.

feedback.pass: Dying out: its usual range ends at 2.
feedback.wrong: Show the whole row, with all four columns, for the one story whose upper end is 4 or lower.

close.finding: Coin flip and Thriving can give 5 of 6: it is inside their usual ranges. Dying out almost never does. So 5 of 6 does not fit the dying out story. A fit is not proof.
